proposals.rationale: Single job with one worker where the only job is cancelled while it is being worked on. The normal finish and the cancellation overlap, so faulty handling can leave the job as finished instead of cancelled or make it runnable again after cancellation.

Single job with two workers where the only job is cancelled while it is being worked on. The idle worker keeps polling while the owner works and the cancellation arrives, so faulty claim handling can hand the cancelled job to the second worker or let it run twice.

Two jobs with one worker where the waiting second job is cancelled while the first job is being worked on. This separates cancellation of a queued job from cancellation of a running job and can reveal a mix-up that lets the cancelled queued job run or disturbs the running job.

Two jobs with two workers where both jobs are cancelled after claims have started. With claims, finishes and cancellations all overlapping, faulty handling can let a cancelled job finish as normal, run on both workers, or disturb the other job.

Three jobs with two workers and a high retry allowance where two jobs are cancelled while work is in progress. The extra queued work plus retry counting widens the window where a late finish can undo a cancellation or where cancellation can harm the state of a job that should keep running.

Three jobs with one worker where every job is cancelled after work has started. The worker must wind down without finishing any cancelled job as done and without making any of them runnable again, which exposes finishes that hide a cancellation.
